newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Romania to work for European integration.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Romania to work for European integration.

text.p: The Polish and Romanian presidents agreed on Monday that the two countries would boost economic and political relations and cooperate in their efforts to join the European Union and NATO.

"We have agreed to build a strong bridge between Poland and Romania...and enhance regional cooperation, which will serve European integration," Romanian President Emil Constantinescu said after meeting his counterpart Aleksander Kwasniewski.

"We would like to strengthen economic, cultural, tourist and sport cooperation," Kwasniewski told a joint news conference in Warsaw. He said experts from both countries would meet to work out concrete measures.
Kwasniewski promised that Poland would back Romania's bid to join the Central European Free Trade Agreement, which also groups the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia.
Constantinescu's two-day visit is his first official foreign trip since his election in November last year, when he defeated ex-communist Ion Iliescu.

He was scheduled to meet Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and other top state officials and will also address a joint meeting of the foreign affairs committees of both houses of parliament, before leaving Warsaw early on Wednesday.
